### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|btc_price_satoshi|number|false|none|For Bitcoin transactions, the price of the buyer's order in satoshi (100 million satoshi equals 1 BTC).|
|btc_receive_address|string|false|none|For Bitcoin transactions, the address that the buyer sent Bitcoin to.|
|buyer_email|string|false|none|The email address of the order's buyer.|
|buyer_note|string|false|none|A note provided by the buyer when the order was created, if any.|
|canceled_note|string|false|none|A note provided by the merchant when the order's state was set to CANCELED, if any.|
|completed_note|string|false|none|A note provided by the merchant when the order's state was set to COMPLETED, if any|
|created_at|string|false|none|The time when the order was created, in ISO 8601 format.|
|errors|[[Error](#schemaerror)]|false|none|Any errors that occurred during the request.|
|expires_at|string|false|none|The time when the order expires if no action is taken, in ISO 8601 format.|
|id|string|false|none|The order's unique identifier.|
|order_history|[[V1OrderHistoryEntry](#schemav1orderhistoryentry)]|false|none|The history of actions associated with the order.|
|payment_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the payment associated with the order.|
|promo_code|string|false|none|The promo code provided by the buyer, if any.|
|recipient_name|string|false|none|The name of the order's buyer.|
|recipient_phone_number|string|false|none|The phone number to use for the order's delivery.|
|refunded_note|string|false|none|A note provided by the merchant when the order's state was set to REFUNDED, if any.|
|shipping_address|[Address](#schemaaddress)|false|none|Represents a postal address in a country. The address format is based <br>on an [open-source library from Google](https://github.com/google/libaddressinput). For more information, <br>see [AddressValidationMetadata](https://github.com/google/libaddressinput/wiki/AddressValidationMetadata). <br>This format has dedicated fields for four address components: postal code, <br>locality (city), administrative district (state, prefecture, or province), and <br>sublocality (town or village). These components have dedicated fields in the <br>`Address` object because software sometimes behaves differently based on them. <br>For example, sales tax software may charge different amounts of sales tax <br>based on the postal code, and some software is only available in <br>certain states due to compliance reasons.<br><br>For the remaining address components, the `Address` type provides the <br>`address_line_1` and `address_line_2` fields for free-form data entry. <br>These fields are free-form because the remaining address components have <br>too many variations around the world and typical software does not parse <br>these components. These fields enable users to enter anything they want. <br><br>Note that, in the current implementation, all other `Address` type fields are blank. <br>These include `address_line_3`, `sublocality_2`, `sublocality_3`, <br>`administrative_district_level_2`, `administrative_district_level_3`, <br>`first_name`, `last_name`, and `organization`. <br><br>When it comes to localization, the seller's language preferences <br>(see [Language preferences](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/locations-api#location-specific-and-seller-level-language-preferences)) <br>are ignored for addresses. Even though Square products (such as Square Point of Sale <br>and the Seller Dashboard) mostly use a seller's language preference in <br>communication, when it comes to addresses, they will use English for a US address, <br>Japanese for an address in Japan, and so on.|
|state|string|false|none|Whether the tax is an ADDITIVE tax or an INCLUSIVE tax.|
|subtotal_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|tender|[V1Tender](#schemav1tender)|false|none|A tender represents a discrete monetary exchange. Square represents this<br>exchange as a money object with a specific currency and amount, where the<br>amount is given in the smallest denomination of the given currency.<br><br>Square POS can accept more than one form of tender for a single payment (such<br>as by splitting a bill between a credit card and a gift card). The `tender`<br>field of the Payment object lists all forms of tender used for the payment.<br><br>Split tender payments behave slightly differently from single tender payments:<br><br>The receipt_url for a split tender corresponds only to the first tender listed<br>in the tender field. To get the receipt URLs for the remaining tenders, use<br>the receipt_url fields of the corresponding Tender objects.<br><br>*A note on gift cards**: when a customer purchases a Square gift card from a<br>merchant, the merchant receives the full amount of the gift card in the<br>associated payment.<br><br>When that gift card is used as a tender, the balance of the gift card is<br>reduced and the merchant receives no funds. A `Tender` object with a type of<br>`SQUARE_GIFT_CARD` indicates a gift card was used for some or all of the<br>associated payment.|
|total_discount_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|total_price_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|total_shipping_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|total_tax_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|updated_at|string|false|none|The time when the order was last modified, in ISO 8601 format.|

A payment represents a paid transaction between a Square merchant and a
customer. Payment details are usually available from Connect API endpoints
within a few minutes after the transaction completes.

Each Payment object includes several fields that end in `_money`. These fields
describe the various amounts of money that contribute to the payment total:

<ul>
<li>
Monetary values are <b>positive</b> if they represent an
<em>increase</em> in the amount of money the merchant receives (e.g.,
<code>tax_money</code>, <code>tip_money</code>).
</li>
<li>
Monetary values are <b>negative</b> if they represent an
<em>decrease</em> in the amount of money the merchant receives (e.g.,
<code>discount_money</code>, <code>refunded_money</code>).
</li>
</ul>

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|additive_tax|[[V1PaymentTax](#schemav1paymenttax)]|false|none|All of the additive taxes associated with the payment.|
|additive_tax_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|created_at|string|false|none|The time when the payment was created, in ISO 8601 format. Reflects the time of the first payment if the object represents an incomplete partial payment, and the time of the last or complete payment otherwise.|
|creator_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the Square account that took the payment.|
|device|[Device](#schemadevice)|false|none|none|
|discount_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|gross_sales_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|id|string|false|none|The payment's unique identifier.|
|inclusive_tax|[[V1PaymentTax](#schemav1paymenttax)]|false|none|All of the inclusive taxes associated with the payment.|
|inclusive_tax_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|is_partial|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether or not the payment is only partially paid for.<br>If true, this payment will have the tenders collected so far, but the<br>itemizations will be empty until the payment is completed.|
|itemizations|[[V1PaymentItemization](#schemav1paymentitemization)]|false|none|The items purchased in the payment.|
|merchant_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the merchant that took the payment.|
|net_sales_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|net_total_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|payment_url|string|false|none|The URL of the payment's detail page in the merchant dashboard. The merchant must be signed in to the merchant dashboard to view this page.|
|processing_fee_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|receipt_url|string|false|none|The URL of the receipt for the payment. Note that for split tender<br>payments, this URL corresponds to the receipt for the first tender<br>listed in the payment's tender field. Each Tender object has its own<br>receipt_url field you can use to get the other receipts associated with<br>a split tender payment.|
|refunded_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|refunds|[[V1Refund](#schemav1refund)]|false|none|All of the refunds applied to the payment. Note that the value of all refunds on a payment can exceed the value of all tenders if a merchant chooses to refund money to a tender after previously accepting returned goods as part of an exchange.|
|surcharge_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|surcharges|[[V1PaymentSurcharge](#schemav1paymentsurcharge)]|false|none|A list of all surcharges associated with the payment.|
|swedish_rounding_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|tax_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|tender|[[V1Tender](#schemav1tender)]|false|none|All of the tenders associated with the payment.|
|tip_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|total_collected_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|

Payment include an` itemizations` field that lists the items purchased,
along with associated fees, modifiers, and discounts. Each itemization has an
`itemization_type` field that indicates which of the following the itemization
represents:

<ul>
<li>An item variation from the merchant's item library</li>
<li>A custom monetary amount</li>
<li>
An action performed on a Square gift card, such as activating or
reloading it.
</li>
</ul>

*Note**: itemization information included in a `Payment` object reflects
details collected **at the time of the payment**. Details such as the name or
price of items might have changed since the payment was processed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|discount_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|discounts|[[V1PaymentDiscount](#schemav1paymentdiscount)]|false|none|All discounts applied to this itemization.|
|gross_sales_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|item_detail|[V1PaymentItemDetail](#schemav1paymentitemdetail)|false|none|V1PaymentItemDetail|
|item_variation_name|string|false|none|The name of the item variation purchased, if any.|
|itemization_type|string|false|none|The type of purchase that the itemization represents, such as an ITEM or CUSTOM_AMOUNT|
|modifiers|[[V1PaymentModifier](#schemav1paymentmodifier)]|false|none|All modifier options applied to this itemization.|
|name|string|false|none|The item's name.|
|net_sales_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|notes|string|false|none|Notes entered by the merchant about the item at the time of payment, if any.|
|quantity|number|false|none|The quantity of the item purchased. This can be a decimal value.|
|single_quantity_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|taxes|[[V1PaymentTax](#schemav1paymenttax)]|false|none|All taxes applied to this itemization.|
|total_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_V1Tender">V1Tender</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemav1tender"></a>
<a id="schema_V1Tender"></a>
<a id="tocSv1tender"></a>
<a id="tocsv1tender"></a>

```json
{
  "card_brand": "string",
  "change_back_money": {
    "amount": 0,
    "currency_code": "string"
  },
  "employee_id": "string",
  "entry_method": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "is_exchange": true,
  "name": "string",
  "pan_suffix": "string",
  "payment_note": "string",
  "receipt_url": "string",
  "refunded_money": {
    "amount": 0,
    "currency_code": "string"
  },
  "settled_at": "string",
  "tendered_at": "string",
  "tendered_money": {
    "amount": 0,
    "currency_code": "string"
  },
  "total_money": {
    "amount": 0,
    "currency_code": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

A tender represents a discrete monetary exchange. Square represents this
exchange as a money object with a specific currency and amount, where the
amount is given in the smallest denomination of the given currency.

Square POS can accept more than one form of tender for a single payment (such
as by splitting a bill between a credit card and a gift card). The `tender`
field of the Payment object lists all forms of tender used for the payment.

Split tender payments behave slightly differently from single tender payments:

The receipt_url for a split tender corresponds only to the first tender listed
in the tender field. To get the receipt URLs for the remaining tenders, use
the receipt_url fields of the corresponding Tender objects.

*A note on gift cards**: when a customer purchases a Square gift card from a
merchant, the merchant receives the full amount of the gift card in the
associated payment.

When that gift card is used as a tender, the balance of the gift card is
reduced and the merchant receives no funds. A `Tender` object with a type of
`SQUARE_GIFT_CARD` indicates a gift card was used for some or all of the
associated payment.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|card_brand|string|false|none|The brand of credit card provided.|
|change_back_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|employee_id|string|false|none|The ID of the employee that processed the tender.|
|entry_method|string|false|none|The tender's unique ID.|
|id|string|false|none|The tender's unique ID.|
|is_exchange|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether or not the tender is associated with an exchange. If is_exchange is true, the tender represents the value of goods returned in an exchange not the actual money paid. The exchange value reduces the tender amounts needed to pay for items purchased in the exchange.|
|name|string|false|none|A human-readable description of the tender.|
|pan_suffix|string|false|none|The last four digits of the provided credit card's account number.|
|payment_note|string|false|none|Notes entered by the merchant about the tender at the time of payment, if any. Typically only present for tender with the type: OTHER.|
|receipt_url|string|false|none|The URL of the receipt for the tender.|
|refunded_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|settled_at|string|false|none|The time when the tender was settled, in ISO 8601 format.|
|tendered_at|string|false|none|The time when the tender was created, in ISO 8601 format.|
|tendered_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|total_money|[V1Money](#schemav1money)|false|none|none|
|type|string|false|none|The type of tender.|

|version|integer|false|none|Used for resolving concurrency issues. The request fails if the version<br>provided does not match the server version at the time of the request. If not provided,<br>Square executes a blind write, potentially overwriting data from another write. For more information,<br>see [optimistic concurrency](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/working-with-apis/optimistic-concurrency).|

Sets the day of the week and hour of the day that a business starts a
workweek. This is used to calculate overtime pay.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_at|string|false|none|A read-only timestamp in RFC 3339 format; presented in UTC.|
|id|string|false|none|The UUID for this object.|
|start_of_day_local_time|string|true|none|The local time at which a business week ends. Represented as a<br>string in `HH:MM` format (`HH:MM:SS` is also accepted, but seconds are<br>truncated).|
|start_of_week|string|true|none|The day of the week on which a business week ends for<br>compensation purposes.|
|updated_at|string|false|none|A read-only timestamp in RFC 3339 format; presented in UTC.|
|version|integer|false|none|Used for resolving concurrency issues. The request fails if the version<br>provided does not match the server version at the time of the request. If not provided,<br>Square executes a blind write; potentially overwriting data from another<br>write.|
